However, they do mention that the plant flooded on May 21, 2026, and that Corvane released two modules from undamaged stock, with the replacement Units expected to ship on June 8 and arrive on June 10, 2026 [2][2].

Additionally, Apex claimed that the flood at Corvane's plant was a Force Majeure Event, and that the delay in delivering the replacement Units was caused by this event [3].

The documents do not provide a specific date for when the plant reopened.

turns.question: What rate of interest can Morgan charge Apex on unpaid liquidated damages?
turns.text:
The Services Agreement specifies that if Delivery is not complete by the Delivery Date, the Supplier shall pay the Buyer liquidated damages of one percent (1%) of the Total Contract Price for each week of delay [3].

However, Amendment No. 1 to the Services Agreement amends clause 7.1 to increase the liquidated damages rate to one and one-half percent (1.5%) of the Total Contract Price for each week of delay [7].

This amendment was signed on May 14, 2026, and takes effect from that date [7].

Therefore, the rate of interest that Morgan can charge Apex on unpaid liquidated damages is 1.5% of the Total Contract Price for each week of delay.
notes: Clause 7.1 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 2.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

turns.question: Which units were rejected, why, and which units replaced them?
turns.text:
The rejected units were Unit IC450-1113 and Unit IC450-1134. Unit IC450-1113 was rejected because of a cracked condenser housing, and Unit IC450-1134 was rejected due to a refrigerant leak at a brazed joint in circuit 2 [3].

The rejected units were replaced by Units IC450-1141 and IC450-1142. These replacement units were delivered to the Delivery Point on June 10, 2026, and passed inspection on June 11, 2026 [1].

turns.question: What delivery date did the Services Agreement originally set?
turns.text:
The Services Agreement (DEMO) originally set the Delivery Date as May 15, 2026. This is stated in the source: [2]

Later, Amendment No. 1 changed the Delivery Date to May 20, 2026. This is stated in the source: [6] Additionally, the source states that the amendment was signed and took effect on May 14, 2026. [6]

The original Delivery Date in the Services Agreement was therefore May 15, 2026, before it was amended.
notes: Clause 4.2 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

turns.question: Is that still the date?
turns.text:
The Delivery Date was amended to May 20, 2026. This is confirmed by Amendment No. 1, which states: "Clause 4.2 of the Services Agreement is deleted and replaced with: '4.2 Delivery Date. The Supplier shall deliver all Units to the Delivery Point on or before May 20, 2026.'" [3] Additionally, the amendment specifies: "Accordingly, the Delivery Date for all purposes of the Agreement, including clauses 7 and 11.3 of the Agreement, is May 20, 2026." [4]

The documents indicate that May 15, 2026, is no longer the Delivery Date. Instead, the amended date is May 20, 2026. [3]
notes: Clause 4.2 of Services Agreement (DEMO) was deleted and replaced by clause 1.1 of Amendment No. 1 (DEMO) (signed). It says: “This Amendment takes effect on May 14, 2026, the date on which it has been signed by both Parties.”

turns.question: What else did that amendment change?
turns.text:
Amendment No. 1 changed the Delivery Date in the Services Agreement from May 15, 2026, to May 20, 2026 [5]. It also modified clause 7.1 to set liquidated damages at 1.5% of the Total Contract Price per week [7].

Other changes included in Amendment No. 1 are the replacement of the original Delivery Date and the adjustment of liquidated damages. However, the cap on liquidated damages in clause 7.2 remained unchanged [8].

Additionally, Amendment No. 1 confirmed that all other terms of the Agreement remain in force [2].

turns.question: When did Apex dispatch the units?
turns.text:
Apex dispatched the units on May 15, 2026, as stated by Apex in its response to the claim. [3]

Witness A also recalled that the units arrived at Dock 3 on May 12, 2026. [2]

However, the delivery was not complete until June 10, 2026, when the replacement units arrived. [1]

The replacement units arrived on June 10, 2026, as confirmed by the gatehouse records. [5]
